scope: One deterministic fixed-reference harmonic segment, its integrated actual residual hazard, its extended first-crossing clock for one threshold, and the pushforward of the Exp(1) marginal. This is a bounded prerequisite for Appendix A.1 (A.1), not the recursive process (A.2) or Proposition 3.1.

expected: A finite-dimensional real Euclidean phase space, represented equivalently by a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel structure.
A scalar potential V, constants alpha, beta, eta, fixed y and reference xRef, and arbitrary phase point z=(x,p).
c=y-eta*gradient(V,xRef), h(x)=gradient(V,x)-gradient(V,xRef).
Phi_s(z)=(c+(x-c)cos(s)+sqrt(eta)*p*sin(s), -eta^(-1/2)*(x-c)sin(s)+p*cos(s)).
lambda(x,p)=sqrt(eta)*max(inner(p,h(x)),0), q(a,s)=lambda(Phi_s(z)).
Lambda(a,t)=integral from 0 to t of q(a,s) ds, with a=(y,xRef,z).
tau(a,e)=inf{u>=0 : e<=Lambda(a,u)}, with empty set represented by infinity.
H(z)=(eta^(-1)*norm(x-c)^2+norm(p)^2)/2 and C(a)=sqrt(eta)*beta*sqrt(2*H(z))*(sqrt(2*eta*H(z))+norm(c-xRef)).
The actual Exp(1) marginal and the actual pushforward under e |-> tau(a,e); any real-to-nonnegative threshold adapter must be justified by Exp(1) support.
The phase point, reference and y vary in the same finite real Hilbert carrier; source R^d has no explicit positive-dimension condition.
The deterministic harmonic flow is defined at all real s. Hazard monotonicity and clock comparisons use nonnegative time.
The deterministic threshold e is nonnegative; a real exponential carrier is allowed only with a support-preserving adapter.
The clock codomain includes infinity, for example WithTop NNReal or an equivalent extended nonnegative carrier.
Every finite time primitive is a finite real integral; infinite waiting time does not imply an infinite finite-time primitive.
For all source-admissible V, alpha, beta and eta; for every fixed y, xRef and arbitrary initial phase point z.
For all nonnegative finite t and all nonnegative deterministic e in the pointwise clock laws.
For each fixed a, push the full actual Exp(1) probability measure forward to the extended clock; the strict survival identity holds for every finite nonnegative t.
No random initial state, iid sequence, random reference draw or independence assumption is required to state the fixed-segment theorem. Those belong to later composition.

literal_source: 0<alpha<=beta and alpha*I <= Hessian(V,x) <= beta*I for every x.
y and xRef are fixed; z is arbitrary. No particular initial-law hypothesis is present in Proposition 3.1's fixed-state boundary.
derived_or_internal_not_public_premises: beta>=0 and eta>0; continuity and beta-Lipschitzness of gradient from the standing regularity/Hessian assumptions.
Joint continuity and nonnegativity of the actual rate along actual Phi; finite-interval integrability and continuity/Borel properties of its primitive.
Existence and attainment of a first crossing when the crossing set is nonempty; order completeness and closedness are proof ingredients.
Flow energy conservation and the exact H(z)-based rate cap.
Exp(1) support, zero atom at zero, exact CDF/survival, probability normalization and measurable pushforward.
assumptions.generalization_discipline: The local one-clock construction needs less than the full paper hypotheses: eta>0 and a continuous beta-Lipschitz gradient suffice for the cap. If the eventual signature drops a source restriction such as eta<=1/beta, this must be recorded as a mathematical generalization with source specialization, not mislabeled literal identity. Conversely, no additional coercivity, higher derivative, cap, integrability, finiteness, positive rank, positive energy, bounded crossing or supplied law premise is permitted merely to close the implementation.
assumptions.endpoint_discipline: The literal source permits eta=1/beta; it implies alpha*eta<=1 and allows equality when alpha=beta. Any alpha*eta restriction must be compared explicitly to the literal eta range.

expected_derived_one_clock_contract: Lambda is jointly continuous/Borel, Lambda(a,0)=0, finite and nonnegative on finite nonnegative time, and nondecreasing there.
The crossing set is empty exactly when tau=infinity; e=0 gives tau=0; e>0 gives tau>0, including the infinity case.
For finite t>=0, tau(a,e)<=t iff e<=Lambda(a,t), with the weak crossing inequality exactly as in (A.1).
If tau is finite, the threshold is attained exactly: Lambda(a,tau)=e. No unconditional finite-wait or strictly increasing hazard conclusion follows.
The clock is jointly Borel, established from finite sublevels; joint continuity of the clock is not expected.

The full pushforward of the actual Exp(1) marginal is a probability law on the extended clock. For every finite t>=0, P(tau>t)=exp(-Lambda(a,t)), expressed as ENNReal.ofReal when using measure values. The strict tail includes infinity.
The actual rate and integrated hazard satisfy q(a,s)<=C(a) and Lambda(a,t)<=C(a)*t, with C computed from the same starting state H(z).
When C(a)>0, e/C(a)<=tau(a,e) as an extended-order inequality. If C(a)=0 and e>0, tau=infinity; e=0 still gives tau=0.
conclusion.literal_versus_bridge: The source explicitly gives (A.1), the empty-set infinity convention, energy, cap, integrated cap and finite-wait lower bound. Joint measurability, exact threshold/attainment laws, the real-to-NNReal adapter and the one-clock survival formula are necessary internal analytic/order/measure bridges derived from these source ingredients; they are not additional displayed source theorems.

expected: Pointwise deterministic laws and a single marginal probability law must stay separate from almost-sure recursive-process claims.
The source phrase 'no jumps' at zero cap is compatible with positive exponential thresholds almost surely. It is not a pointwise claim at the null deterministic threshold e=0.
A zero residual at one phase point gives zero instantaneous rate only; it does not prove that an entire nonconstant orbit has zero hazard.
Rank zero or H(z)=0 may force an entirely zero-rate orbit; these cases must remain legal rather than excluded by a convenience premise.
No refresh intensity or refresh clock is present in Algorithm 1. The Gaussian momentum/reference initialization is not ongoing refresh.
The source bounce has R_0=I and can be discontinuous at zero normal. Clock proofs must not invent global bounce continuity.
The source topology is not a Lean implication graph. Open consumers N25-N30 and independent sequence material do not inherit completion from the one-clock theorem.
lambda has exactly the sqrt(eta) coefficient and positive part of the residual gradient inner product.
The center sign is y-eta*gradient(V,xRef); the flow uses sqrt(eta) and its reciprocal with the specified sine signs.
Energy is the weighted sum of squared norms with coefficient 1/2, not a product-space norm substituted without proof.
The rate cap is exactly sqrt(eta)*beta*sqrt(2*H(z))*(sqrt(2*eta*H(z))+norm(c-xRef)), evaluated on the same orbit's starting energy; it is not a freely supplied cap or an unspecified multiple.
The exponential rate is exactly one, so survival has exp(-Lambda), with no additional rate or normalization constant.
alpha and the paper scale upper bound are standing paper restrictions; they need not enter this local cap formula, and any widened parameter scope must be identified as a generalization.
